title: I'm a little scared to release a game with AI generated code
author: nothing77804
selftext:
I apologise if this has been discussed before or if it's repetitive, but I'd like some insight and help with this.   
I'm making a game. I don't want to disclose the details because I don't really want people to discover that I used AI, but it's a relatively simple game made in SugarCube.   
I've never made a game before. I've had this concept in my head for years but I've never had the time or energy to learn SugarCube/Java/CSS/HTML to make this thing. I'm already studying engineering full time, and the fatigue from Crohn's disease really kicks my ass so I have to budget my energy. 

I'm doing all of the art/icons, ui design, system design, gameplay, and the whole concept is my own. But most of the code is AI generated. I'm not the best at coding. I'd be up for learning but again... time and energy. I can't afford a human dev, but even if I could I'd rather not bring a stranger into my passion project. Several things could go wrong.

I know I'm preaching to the choir here but I just see it as a faster way to get to a better result. I do vigorously playtest the features and make manual edits, so I'm not blindly vibecoding. I think my process is okay for a total beginner?

But I've felt really heavily discouraged lately and I've not touched the game in weeks because I just feel bad. I'm also scared of being harassed and witch hunted. The general attitude I've seen is "if you can't afford to pay others to do things you can't do, and/or cant get investors to fund it, you can't afford to make a game and don't deserve to". 

Has anyone else ever felt like this? How do you deal with it? What's your perspective on this?

comments.author: cckynv
comments.body: Even Steam doesn’t require you to disclose if you used AI to code your game. Unless you’re publicly advertising that you used AI for coding, or providing the source code publicly, no one will be able to tell. I say release your work and don’t worry too much about it, especially if you’re doing all your own art.

replies.author: nothing77804
replies.body: Thank you. I don't plan on disclosing at all, and I just hope no one will start probing me about it. I just get a little paranoid sometimes because I've been around anti AI people that are extremely vitriolic.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: No problem. I think, in general, people are far less concerned about AI-assisted or AI-generated code as they are AI-generated art, and you're not using any of that, so I doubt there will be any probing at all. I understand the paranoia though, anti's can be very vicious and love to witch hunt, but I don't think you will run into any issues at all. The only real way for someone to know you used AI code is if you disclose it.

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
The movement is kind of dumb and misdirected. Really their ire should be drawn to companies who are actually laying off and firing people and replacing them with AI art. But instead they are attacking people who are creating games with AI who otherwise never would have had the means to hire anyone anyway.

But that’s emblematic of this entire decade I feel like. Corporations and the rich somehow successfully redirect anger towards other lower class people away from themselves

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body:
In my opinion, most of the worst anti rhetoric comes from artists or “creatives” who are lashing out at any perceived threat to their skill set and/or income stream. It’s mostly a form of gatekeeping.

But I agree with you in that they should be focusing more on the corporations using it vs targeting individual creators. I think they realize they are far too small a movement to really have any sway over big corps, so they pivoted to targeting the easier target: individuals.

replies.author: Ok-Rush-6379
replies.body: Your game will 100% be decompiled. You are better off to disclose AI usage.

replies.author: Diealiceis
replies.body: You can tell its AI by looking at it though.

replies.author: dksprocket
replies.body: Be aware that if you use your reddit account to advertise the game in Reddit, there's a good chance anti-AI people will Google your username to check if posts in AI subs comes up. Hiding your post history is no guarantee (and generally just looks suspicious).

comments.author: Apalala__
comments.body:
Use a different account with a different alias to release your game.

Use AI to filter the comments and extract only the feedback that actually helps you improve.

And [JUST DO IT](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZXsQAXx_ao0).

replies.author: nothing77804
replies.body:
Icl that video made me smile. Thank you.  
The comment filtering is a good idea. And I already plan to use a different account for it all anyway. I don't feel like becoming a public game dev personality (??) anyway.

comments.author: Russmac316
comments.body:
Gatekeepers, old heads and people who want to be miserable. People defy change like crazy. This lowers the barrier of entry for many people who simply aren't good at it. Overall, it's a good thing for creatives because we now may get unique games we never would've gotten before, but it will also increase the amount of slop tenfold.

I wouldn't worry about it. If your game does well and you make some money, maybe hire someone to oversee the code at that point.

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body:
The irony is most people write this wrom a device using software that uses AI written code. It is everywhere and it will be absolutely be normalized.

Where I have doubts if it will be normalized soon is game art assets. When you are doing all of the art I dont see the problem.

replies.author: nothing77804
replies.body: Yeah art is a whole different beast. I find art to be kind of draining, especially when I'm making clothing and things like that, but I like having my skin attached to my body so I'll push through it.

comments.author: ArchivisX
comments.body: The problem with AI in games isn't the AI, it's that the games are simply not good.  Break the mold, release an enticing game, and it won't matter.

comments.author: Thin-Regular-8807
comments.body: I'd be more worried about the code its self unless checked by a skilled human.

comments.author: mile-high-guy
comments.body: Pretty much all software is written by engineers using AI these days
